verdict.rationale: llama.cpp's README states it supports 1.5-bit through 8-bit integer quantization for reduced memory use, which covers the story's full very-low-bit-to-8-bit range. A community report independently confirms that Q6_K is much smaller than FP16 while nearly matching its perplexity. missing for 10: in-depth first-party documentation of the quantization workflow and tooling, concrete per-format memory-savings figures, independent corroboration for the very-low-bit (1.5–3 bit) formats

support.subject: As a power-user, I can reduce memory footprint using integer quantization ranging from very low-bit to 8-bit precision

citations.quote: 1.5-bit, 2-bit, 3-bit, 4-bit, 5-bit, 6-bit, and 8-bit integer quantization for faster inference and reduced memory use
llama.cpp's Q6_K quantization nearly matches FP16 perplexity while being much smaller
